answer: Like a falcon that must hunt rather than borrow another bird's wings, each agent periodically proves itself by completing verifiable useful work — a computation whose result any peer can re-check cheaply, priced in wall-clock time rather than tokens. A sybil farmer must pay that time cost for every fake identity, so spawning a thousand clones costs a thousand hunts, while honest agents earn standing from one mesa of shared results. The limit: this is no haven for newcomers with weak hardware, and a rich attacker can still rent compute, so work proofs must pair with stake or reputation caps.
